title: Package report
description: POST /api/v1/reports/packages (FR-2.3, P2-S08). Every installed package from the host's package manager. The body may be sent with `Content-Encoding: gzip`. A host whose package manager is not supported says so with `manager: unsupported` and a reason, and a host whose dpkg database could not be listed says so with `manager: unreadable` and a reason; neither sends packages, so neither is ever mistaken for a host with none installed. Packages that exist but are not installed in full (an interrupted installation) are not listed in `packages`; their names are in `skipped`.

schema_version.description: Payload schema version. This directory is version 1.

report_id.description: UUIDv4, generated per report and reused on retry so the server can discard duplicates.

collected_at.description: When the agent collected the facts (agent clock), RFC 3339 UTC.

manager.description: The package manager the agent found. `dpkg` is the only supported one (DEC-01); `unsupported` when the host has another or none; `unreadable` when the host has dpkg but its packages could not be listed.

unsupported_reason.description: Why the packages could not be listed, for the operator, when `manager` is `unsupported` or `unreadable` (required then); `null` when `manager` is `dpkg`. The name is kept from the first version of this contract.

packages.description: Every installed package, in any order; empty when `manager` is `unsupported`. A name and architecture appear at most once.

name.description: Binary package name as dpkg records it (lower case), for example `openssl`.

version.description: Installed version exactly as the package manager records it, with any epoch, for example `1:3.5.1-1+deb13u1`: any printable ASCII without spaces. Compared with dpkg's rules, never as a string (FR-2.4); a version dpkg cannot compare is stored and marked not evaluated, not refused (P2-S09).

source.description: Source package name, which vulnerability data is keyed on (DEC-11); `null` when the package manager records none.

skipped.description: Packages the agent could read the name of but did not list as installed: an interrupted installation (dpkg states `unpacked`, `half-installed`, `half-configured`; a package in `triggers-awaited` or `triggers-pending` is configured and is listed in `packages`), or an entry it could not carry in full. Optional; absent means none. A skipped package is not in the installed set, but the server does not show it as removed (P2-S08). Only names the agent could read are listed; an entry without a readable name is a `warnings` entry.

name.description: Binary package name, with the limits of a package name. No architecture is given: a name covers every architecture of it.

reason.description: Why it was not listed, short, for the operator, for example `half-configured`.

in_use.description: What running processes use (FR-2.6, VT-A01, VT-A02), for vulnerability triage: exposure (N4) and the escalation of packages a listening process loads. Binary package names and classes, never process ids, command lines, or user names; addresses and ports only as the listening sockets in `loaded_by_listeners`. Optional, and only with `manager: dpkg`. Absent or `null` means the agent did not report use (an older agent, or it could not read the sockets or services whole; a `warnings` entry with field `in_use` says why). Every list here is positive evidence only, and nothing is ever called idle from it (owner decision 2026-11-21): a package left out of a list is simply not known to be in use.

listening.description: Each binary package owning the `ExecStart=` executable of a systemd service with a listening TCP socket or bound UDP socket, once, sorted by name: `network` when any of its sockets is on a non-loopback address (including the wildcard), `loopback` when all are on 127.0.0.0/8 or ::1. The package is the command's: a wrapper (`pg_ctlcluster` of `postgresql-common` for PostgreSQL, `sh -c`, `env`, an interpreter) is named, not the program it starts, which the agent cannot see without a new privilege. Positive evidence only.

services.description: The binary packages owning the `ExecStart=` executables of running systemd services, each once, sorted. As in `listening`, a wrapper's package is named. Positive evidence only.

unnamed_listeners.description: Listening or bound sockets the agent counted but could not name a package for: not in a systemd service (a container, a user session, the kernel), or a service whose executable no package owns.

library_scan.description: The optional library-use scan (VT-A02), enabled per VM in the agent's local config: `off` (the default), `ran`, or `failed` (enabled but it gave no result; a `warnings` entry with field `in_use` says why).

libraries.description: With `library_scan: ran`, every binary package that lists a file mapped by a running process (each package that lists it, for a diverted or shared file), once, sorted by name; `stale` when a process still maps a deleted version of one of its files (it runs old code until restarted). Interpreted code (Python, Perl, Ruby, Node, Java) is read, not mapped, so it is listed only when something of it is mapped. Positive evidence only. `null` otherwise.

loaded_by_listeners.description: With `library_scan: ran`, each binary package that lists a file (ELF or not) mapped by a process holding a listening TCP socket or bound UDP socket of the host's network namespace, with that process's program's package (`listener`, `null` when no package owns the program) and `network` when one of the sockets it holds is on a non-loopback address (including the wildcard), else `loopback`. With the listening process's systemd unit (`service`) and the listening sockets it holds (`sockets`, so a triage reason can name them). Each (package, listener, service) once, sorted by package, then listener, then service (`null` first). Positive evidence only: what the scan misses is not listed. `null` otherwise.

listener.description: The package of the listening process's program (`/proc/<pid>/exe`), or `null` when no package owns it.

service.description: The listening process's systemd unit, from its cgroup: a service or socket unit in `system.slice`, or `init.scope` (systemd itself, for socket activation); `null` elsewhere (a container, a user session).

class.description: Where the process's listening sockets are.

sockets.description: The listening sockets those processes hold, `address:port/protocol` (`0.0.0.0:22/tcp`, `[::1]:53/udp`): network ones first, then by text, at most 4. This is the only place the report carries addresses and ports (owner decision 2026-11-21, for the triage reason).

scanned_at.description: When the library scan whose result this is started (agent clock, RFC 3339 UTC). The agent runs it at most once an hour and reuses the last result, or the last failure, in reports made in between, so this can be up to an hour older than `collected_at`. `null` when `library_scan` is `off`.

complete.description: `true` exactly when the library scan ran: `libraries` and `loaded_by_listeners` are then the scan's whole result. `false` when only services were looked at.

warnings.description: Problems reading the package list (field `packages`) or what is in use (field `in_use`), for the operator. What was read is still sent.

field.description: What could not be read in full: the package list, or what is in use.
